covers.quote: Unless it is obvious from the context:
Follow the title with the rest of the citation.

examples.note: Puts the legislation title before the pinpoint provision.

parts.quote: The Loans Security Act 1973 (subsection 5A(b)) provides for ...

examples.note: Puts the legislation title before the pinpoint provision in parentheses.

parts.quote: Commonwealth legislation (Loans Security Act 1973,subsection 5A(b)) provides for ...

examples.note: Places the pinpoint reference before the legislation title.

parts.quote: Commonwealth legislation (subsection 5A(b), Loans Security Act 1973) provides for ...

rules.quote: Put the title first when writing in-text citations, footnotes and endnotes.
rules.violation_condition: an in-text citation, footnote, or endnote citing legislation that places the pinpoint or provision before the legislation title, unless obvious from the context
when: Unless it is obvious from the context.
rules.why: G-2: Consolidated list items specifying order into one rule with its condition.

examples.note: Lists the Act name first in a basic note.

rules.quote: Always list the legislation or case name first in a basic note.
rules.violation_condition: a basic note citing legislation or a legal case that does not list the legislation or case name first
when: In a basic footnote or endnote citing legal material.

covers.quote: In digital content, the reference markers can be hyperlinked to help users access the note.

rules.quote: Use hyperlinked endnotes in digital content.
rules.violation_condition: unlinked reference markers or endnotes in digital content
when: When using endnotes in digital content.
rules.why: Direct instruction on formatting endnotes in digital content.

covers.quote: Include separate reference lists for legal material in 3 situations
People need the list to understand the content.
The content includes a reference list for non-legal sources.
It is agency style to have a reference list.

rules.quote: Most government writers should only include a reference list if one of these applies:
rules.specification: Do not include a separate legal reference list unless required by agency style, accompanied by a non-legal reference list, or essential for understanding.
rules.violation_condition: inclusion of a separate reference list for legal material when none of the three conditions (needed to understand content, non-legal sources list included, or agency style) applies
when: People need the list to understand the content.
The content includes a reference list for non-legal sources.
It is agency style to have a reference list.
rules.why: G-2: absorbed list conditions into single constraint.

examples.note: Lists are divided under separate subheadings.

rules.quote: Set up separate lists under the subheadings ‘Legislation’ and ‘Legal cases’.
rules.violation_condition: a legal reference list that combines legislation and cases under one heading or does not use the subheadings 'Legislation' and 'Legal cases'
when: When including a reference list for legal material.
rules.why: Structural requirement for legal reference lists.

rules.quote: Arrange legislation and legal cases in alphabetical order under these headings.
rules.violation_condition: legislation or legal cases in a reference list not sorted in alphabetical order
when: When listing legislation or legal cases under reference list subheadings.

examples.note: Titles are formatted in roman type rather than italics.

parts.quote: Dutton v Republic of South Africa [1999] FCA 2

rules.quote: Write the titles of Acts and legal cases in roman type, even though they’re italicised in the text.
rules.violation_condition: titles of Acts or legal cases italicised in a reference list
rules.why: Typography rule specifically for legal reference lists.
